title: feat(spec)!: addRecord says what renders — enabled required, position top, mode/formView retired
body:
Closes #24692
Clause-②: yes (narrowing: `mode` / `formView` retire through ADR-0087 drop conversions; `enabled` becomes required)

A list's `addRecord` block now says what the renderer draws. `enabled` is required with no default, `position` defaults to `top`, and `mode` / `formView` are retired through the `spec-property-retirement` kit. It ships in 18.x under the standing ruling for breaking narrowings after GA (#6015, comment 6292005854, 「甲」), because ADR-0087 conversions cover every body that parsed under 18.0.

## The ruling this implements (comment 6281834942, letter B′, items 1–5 verbatim)

> 1. `AddRecordConfigSchema` (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, the same schema on the page `list-view` node) keeps two keys: `enabled`, REQUIRED with no default, so `addRecord: {}` is refused at authoring and at publish instead of drawing nothing; and `position`, default `top`, values `top` / `bottom` / `both` as the renderer draws them.
>
> 2. `mode` and `formView` retire through the `spec-property-retirement` kit: ADR-0087 conversion entries that drop the two keys from authored and stored bodies with a notice, `retiredKey()` tombstones on the strict object, the two form composites (`view.form.ts:178`, `page.form.ts:165`), regenerated artifacts, the liveness ledger. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, breaking, with its ADR-0087 disposition and the FROM → TO in the changeset.
>
> 3. The producers follow in the same PR: showcase `active-projects.page.ts:36`, `contact.view.ts:60` and the lint fixture `showcase-shape.fixtures.ts:414` lose `mode` / `formView`; `content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx:88` states the convention of item 4 and names no binding — the docs line is part of the retirement kit's surface and is declared in the claim as a cross-domain file.
>
> 4. objectui: the create entry selects `formViews.create` when the object declares it, else today's `form` / `formViews.default` (`app-shell/src/utils/recordFormNavigation.ts:218`, one selection line, pinned by a test). objectstack-ai/objectui#13099 is that card; its parity row (`p1-spec-alignment.test.ts:189`, the `mode` default) changes when objectui's pin takes the spec release.
>
> 5. ADR-0050 (Proposed) Decision 2 gains a dated note that the list add-record open mode is no longer declared on `addRecord`; how the create form opens stays the renderer's, and a per-list open mode, if ever wanted, is the list's existing `navigation.mode`, never a second enum. Tier H; it may ride the spec PR (the PR is then Tier H whole) or go as its own one-line PR — the spec seat chooses.

## What changed

**Schema (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, `AddRecordConfigSchema`).** One def serves every door: `ListViewSchema`, `ObjectListViewSchema` (an object's or a container's `listViews`), `InterfacePageConfigSchema` (a list page's `interfaceConfig`) and the page `list-view` node's props row.
- `enabled` is `z.boolean()` with no default. If the key is omitted, the parse refuses with a prescription that names the key and says how to fix it.
- `position` defaults to `top`. The values `top` / `bottom` / `both` are unchanged. I checked the renderer at objectui origin/main and at the pinned sha `616df6598b`: `ListView.tsx#resolveAddRecordPlacement` maps an absent position to top, and `showAddRecord` needs `enabled === true`.
- `mode` and `formView` are `retiredKey()` tombstones. Authoring either key is a `tsc` error and also a parse error that carries the prescription.

**ADR-0087.** There are two D2 conversions, both retired from the load path with `retiredAfter: '18.0.0'`.
- They reach `stack.views[]` in all three persisted spellings, `objects[].listViews.*`, `pages[].interfaceConfig` and every page `list-view` node.
- `add-record-mode-form-view-removed` strips both keys and emits one notice per key.
- `add-record-enabled-defaulted` writes `enabled: true` onto a block that omits `enabled`. An explicit value is never touched.
- `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `ui/AddRecordConfig:mode` and `ui/AddRecordConfig:formView`.
- The D3 entries are `add-record-mode-form-view-retired` and `add-record-enabled-required`. Each has its own step-18 rationale fragment.
- The two default moves are declared in `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR[18]`.

**Ruling item 3 under 「甲」: the `enabled` half ships with a conversion, not as a warning.** I measured whether any producer writes `addRecord` without `enabled`:
- this repository at `71696121a6`: the showcase's two blocks and the lint fixture all write `enabled: true`;
- objectui's Studio design surface at the pin: it writes `addRecord: { enabled: true }`;
- production databases: not measured.

The measured population is zero, so the conversion is sound. It is lossless against the contract, because it writes the value the 18.0 parse already produced. It is not lossless in pixels, and the changeset says so: a stored block that omitted `enabled` drew no button, and once converted it draws the one it declared. No 19.0 refusal card is needed.

**Forms.** In `view.form.ts` and `page.form.ts`, the `addRecord` composites now list `enabled` and `position` explicitly. The new nested labels are translated in the three locales.

**Liveness ledger.** The `liveness/view.json` `addRecord` row records the removal. The sub-keys are one drill level below a recorded undrilled container, so no row is added or removed. The README residue line is updated.

**Producers and docs.**
- showcase `contact.view.ts` and `active-projects.page.ts`, and the lint fixture `showcase-shape.fixtures.ts`, drop `mode` / `formView`.
- `content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx` states the convention (`formViews.create` when declared, else `form` / `formViews.default`) and names no binding.
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx` drops `addRecord.formView` from where a named form is served and states the `create` convention.
- `@objectstack/lint`: `os explain list-view-field-unknown` and one docblock no longer name `addRecord.formView`. `lintViewRefs` never read it.
- The reference pages under `content/docs/references/` are regenerated.

**Tests.**
- New `packages/spec/src/ui/add-record-config-retirement.test.ts`, in the repo project. It covers every door, the prescriptions, the `tsc` channel, the conversions over stored view, page and object rows, idempotence, load-path retirement, the ledger rows, the forms, and a tree-scoped absence pin over the five declared roots.
- `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` joins both new conversions.
- The old `view.test.ts` / `page.test.ts` pins on `mode` and the `bottom` default are rewritten.

## Not in this PR
- **ADR-0050 Decision 2 note:** a Tier H file, so it goes in its own one-line PR (ruling item 5). The exact text is in the dev report.
- **objectui** (ruling item 4) is objectstack-ai/objectui#13099, which is already closed. Its `p1-spec-alignment.test.ts:189` parity row (`mode` default `inline`) will go red when objectui's pin takes this spec release, and ruling item 4 says that row changes then. No objectui source writes `mode` or `formView` at the pin (`git grep` at `616df6598b`).
- `content/docs/releases/` is untouched.

## Acceptance notes
- The showcase's `active-projects.page.ts` sets `userActions.addRecordForm: false` next to `addRecord: { enabled: true }`. objectui's `ListView` withholds the Add button on `addRecordForm === false`, so that page probably shows no Add button, even though its comment says it shows one. I only read this from the code and did not reproduce it in a browser, so it is not filed. Carrier: none.
- The 18.0 parse materialized `position: 'bottom'` into built artifacts that carried an `addRecord` block. Those artifacts keep `bottom` explicitly, so nothing moves on screen for them.
